Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court was a district and trial court in the county of Galveston, Texas, built in 1869 and the first session was held in 1878. This court serves the residents of the 104th largest county Galveston in Texas states. The court administrator manages all court things. The court has jurisdiction over criminal, civil and family matters, Traffic and Vehicle Matters or small claim matters.

How to search for the case record?

Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court records information for any case is available at the court office in files, on the computer, and online. They can be found online by using the following ways:

  • Searching by name
  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Some information about cases is not available online because they are confidential by law, like harassment, criminal offense, etc. These types of information are only available at the court office. You had to submit a form for this information by visiting the court, and then the court would respond whether to provide the record information or not. Mostly confidential information is only given to the person involved in the case or to the police or investigation agency. There is no cost for searching records.

What is the eligibility for a defendant to receive a virtual court appearance?

Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court virtual court was introduced during coronavirus, and the online hearing can be done using zoom. If you attend a virtual court appearance, then you are eligible for the following:

  • Enter a plea of guilty. The court will respond to you with the schedule and the zoom link for the online hearing.
  • Enter a plea of not guilty and request a trial by a judge. A trial schedule notice will be sent to you by the court.
  • You can request an extension on the payment.
  • Look for the resolution of warrants for outstanding Clear Lake Shores.

What are the rules that are followed in the trial information?

Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court trial contains a complaint document that alleged the act you committed. In all trials, objections are presented to the state attorney or prosecutor. The rules follow for the trial information are:

  • Procedure for trial
  • Trial by Bench or Jury
  • Pro se Parties
  • Resets for Trials

How to make payments?

Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court payments required items are ticket number and acceptable amount. The payments for tickets and fines can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for traffic tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter. 2.99% convince and other charges will be applied if you pay with a credit card.

Online

A Person can make payment online using a credit card through an automated system. A citation number is needed for online payment. A nominal fee, including the convenience fees, will occur.

Phone

Payment can be made by phone using the number 1-800-444-1187. Tell the citation number, and the cost will be paid. Charges will be applied in this method.

How many types of pleas does a person send to the court?

The American System of Justice introduces the Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court plea. You had to decide which request to enter carefully. Three types of pleas are available in this court:

Plea of Guilty

In a guilty plea, you confess that you broke the law or committed that crime and feel no excuse for your act. In this plea, a court hearing with fines is held against you. This plea can be used against you in a civil suit.

Plea of No Consent

Plea of no consent means you do not consent to the state's charges against you. You were found guilty and had to complete a safety driving course or court-ordered probation for eligibility. It is not used against you in a civil suit for damage.

Plea of Not Guilty

In a plea of not guilty, you deny that you committed a crime, and the state will prove that crime or charges against you. In this case, the decision to hire an attorney will be up to you. If you fight your case by yourself, a trial section on the website will help you understand the procedure.

What will a juvenile have to do if a charge is against them?

In Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court, if a charge is against a juvenile, they must appear in court with the parents or guardian. A warrant is issued with an additional fine if they do not appear in court on the schedule. Juveniles cannot get a driver's license unless they appear in court. If a person under 21 is charged with the drug alcohol, they have to appear before the judge in open court.

When will the request for grant continuance be accepted?

Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court grant continuance request will be accepted if the reasons are the following:

  • Death of a family member
  • Medical condition or reason
  • Went out of town due to work or personal reason
  • Any religious event where court proceeding events are prohibited

FAQ:

What is the eligibility for enrolling in the driving safety course?

Clear Lake Shores Municipal Court offers a driving safety course for the person who had charges against them. The enrollment eligibility is that your age must be 18+ or up to 55. You must be charged with a crime or traffic violation. Payment should be made before the course starts. You also get a certificate if you complete the course and your fines will also be reduced.

How can I attend my virtual court hearing?

You had to use the zoom application for the virtual hearing. The court provides a link to you, and you can join the hearing with that link. The Internet is mandatory for the hearing.

When will my pretrial conferences be held?

Your pretrial conferences will be held the same day as the first court appearance.

What is the dress code of the court?

Proper dress code must be followed in the court hearing. The dress should be respectable and not tight. Sleeveless and torn clothes are not allowed. The judges recommend pent coats and business suits.

When will the hearing court hold?

The court hearing will be held on every Wednesday at 1:00 pm.
